# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 7 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 7 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_007_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 7

**7:1** When the child was two years old, Joachim said to Anna: "Let us bring her up to the temple of the Lord, that we may fulfill the vow we vowed, lest the Lord send something untoward upon us and our offering be unacceptable to him."

**7:2** And Anna said, "Let us wait until the third year, so that the child may not seek after her father or mother." And Joachim said, "Let us wait then."

**7:3** And when the child was three years old, Joachim said: "Let us call the undefiled daughters of the Hebrews, and let each one take a burning lamp, so that the child may not turn back and her heart be enticed away from the temple of the Lord."

**7:4** And they did so until they went up into the temple of the Lord. The priest received her and kissed her and blessed her, saying: "The Lord God has magnified your name in all generations. In you the Lord shall reveal his redemption to the children of Israel in the last days."

**7:5** And he set her on the third step of the altar, and the Lord God put grace upon her, and she danced with her feet, and all the house of Israel loved her.

---

## Translator's Note

The procession of virgin torch-bearers (7:3) became one of the most painted scenes in Byzantine art — the Presentation of Mary. The image of the three-year-old dancing before God on the altar steps (7:5) is theologically freighted: it echoes David dancing before the ark, presenting the child Mary as a new ark of the covenant. The priest's prophecy in 7:4 is the first explicit identification of Mary as the instrument of Israel's redemption.
